bottom_line: UT0184000 now has a production-usable custom footprint built from the live official UTA GTFS feed, the official station-address inventory, the official non-LDS park-and-ride inventory, exact official UTA park-and-ride polygons, and exact official FrontRunner platform polygons where available.

doctrine_basis.scope_rule: Use a custom transit-network-and-facilities footprint rather than county or place polygons.

official_scope_evidence.summary: UTA police responsibility is tied to UTA vehicles, property, stations, facilities, parking lots, rail lines, and adjacent stop areas rather than member-county polygons.

geometry_components.station_component_logic: Use exact official FrontRunner platform polygons for in-service FrontRunner stations. For all other official station-inventory rows, match the official station to active GTFS station stop coordinates and buffer the matched stop cluster by 60 m.
geometry_components.park_component_logic: Use exact official UTA Park_and_Ride_Polygons features, but only for facilities present in the non-LDS sections of the official Park and Ride Lots page.

residual_caveats: UTA does not expose a public exact polygon layer for all non-FrontRunner station campuses. TRAX, S-Line, UVX, and Ogden Express station areas are therefore represented by 60 m buffers around the official-station inventory locations matched to active GTFS station stop clusters.
The active GTFS route component is a thin corridor proxy for vehicle-in-service geography, not a claim that UTA owns or controls the full roadway width along bus routes.

The official park-and-ride polygon layer includes LDS and other unsupported rows; this build explicitly restricts park polygons to facilities listed in the non-LDS sections of the official Park and Ride Lots page.

A few official facility labels differ across sources, such as 'Draper Towne Center' versus 'Draper Town Center' and 'River Trail Station*' versus 'River Trail [except Sundays]'; those cross-source aliases are recorded explicitly in this packet.
